decisive_items: Further history elicited pica and exposure to two dogs and a cat.
an absolute eosinophil count of 1,570 cells/µL (normal 40–190)
Chest computed tomography revealed multiple pulmonary nodules with adjacent ground-glass opacities.
response.rationale: The combination of eosinophilia, pulmonary nodules, pica, and animal exposure strongly suggests toxocariasis (visceral larva migrans), which can cause myocarditis and pericardial effusion. Viral myopericarditis and Mycoplasma are less likely given the eosinophilia and negative PCR.

rejected.why: Working diagnosis of viral myopericarditis does not explain the marked eosinophilia, pulmonary nodules, or pica/animal exposure.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection is unlikely because nasopharyngeal PCR was negative and eosinophilia is not typical.
Loeffler syndrome is a nonspecific eosinophilic pulmonary condition and does not account for the cardiac involvement and exposure history as well as toxocariasis.
Duplicate of toxocariasis (R4); the more standard label is chosen.
